title: Define root algorithm registry and fail-closed capability contract
body:
## Outcome
Implement PKI-specific algorithm registry and typed capability report for Ed25519, P-256, RSA-4096, and standardized ML-DSA-44, covering key encoding, certificate/CRL signing and verification, CSR, CMS, and path verification independently. RSA-2048 is compatibility-only behind an explicit policy gate. No implementation is proposed for V1; this is V2 synthetic work.

## Current evidence
Intake census says V1 has no Fleet cert/pki domain. Public crate docs are evidence only for the named version/API surface, not Fleet integration. Use source-backed results in `research/pki-standards.md`; re-check pinned versions when implementing.

## Boundaries and acceptance
Own only PKI algorithm metadata and capability dispatch; reuse the shared adapter seam proposed under #9157 rather than duplicating it. Produce a versioned per-operation matrix and synthetic smoke fixtures. A requested operation succeeds only when the exact adapter/version claims and proves it; independent verification is required for supported signatures. Oracle: adapter test result + independent verifier result, not parser success.

## Negative tests
Reject Dilithium2 as ML-DSA-44, unknown OID, absent primitive, unsupported key parameters, silent RSA-2048 substitution, unsupported ML-DSA client path, and provider-version mismatch.

## Safety and rollback
No production keys or provider writes. Any operator probe strictly parses all declared args before subprocess/network/write/lock; unknown args cause no side effects. Rollback disables the new registry entry/feature and preserves the diagnostic/test corpus; no serialized production state exists.

title: Implement PKI opaque identity, serial ledger, and manifest schema
body:
## Outcome
Implement PKI object metadata for opaque stable IDs, issuer-scoped serial reservation, and versioned manifests. Identity is independent of subject/display name, filesystem path, DNS name, provider-native ID and logical secret path; paths remain mutable locators/attributes. Keep this PKI certificate/serial model scoped to CA artifacts and reference #9157 for the shared opaque ID contract.

## Current evidence
V1 has no Fleet PKI. Spec §§5 and 7 describe IDs, serials and manifest; architecture review ADR-S01 requires stable opaque identity. Do not duplicate generic secret identity or storage work.

## Acceptance/oracle
Golden/property tests prove path/name changes do not change object ID, public/private manifest projections are deterministic and secret-free, and serial reservation is unique per issuer under concurrent synthetic requests. Manifest includes algorithm, key/cert IDs, parent, generation/partition/revision, DER/fingerprint, issuer, serial, SKI/AKI, validity, policy, provenance, public/private file index and validation receipts. Oracle: schema validation, stable canonical bytes, collision oracle and concurrency test.

## Negative tests
Reject ID derived from path/name, duplicate or nonpositive serial, out-of-range serial, path traversal, unknown schema/critical field, tampered hash, and private handle leakage. Do not assume portable CAS; guard levels are declared per adapter-operation and race tests do not treat lease/readback as serialization.

## Rollback
V2 fixtures only; migration rollback retains prior schema/ledger fixtures and uses a new schema version. Scripts validate whole argv before side effects. No provider or production write.

title: Generate four independent synthetic self-signed root identities
body:
## Outcome
Generate an isolated synthetic set with exactly four independent root keys/certificates: Ed25519, P-256, RSA-4096 and ML-DSA-44. Reference notAfter is exactly `2050-07-07T12:00:00Z`; ordinary default remains 20 calendar years. No V1 implementation, production key generation, or live root ceremony.

## Current evidence
V1 intake has no PKI. Spec §§3.1/24.3 and Appendix A PKI-001/PKI2-002 define the reference. Root custody and live execution remain unauthorized.

## Acceptance/oracle
Four distinct synthetic SPKIs/key identities and self-signed certs; exact signature/key algorithm OIDs and validity; subject default `C=US,O=developing.today LLC` and unique CA CN; CA extensions and SKI/AKI; manifest fingerprints and hashes match emitted bytes. Validate signatures and profiles using OpenSSL and independent capable Rust verifier; unsupported algorithm is reported unsupported.

## Negative tests
Reject reused key/SPKI, wrong algorithm or OID, RSA-2048 default, wrong timestamp, invalid CA constraints/usage, bad self-signature and unknown extension.

## Rollback/safety
Only operation-owned synthetic fixture directory may be removed after ownership/hash check; never broad cleanup. Any script validates complete argv before writes/subprocess/network/lock. No live stores, signer, DNS or trust changes.

title: Construct and validate the nine-certificate asymmetric root graph
body:
## Outcome
Create six directed cross-certificates among the three classical roots plus three classical-root-signed ML-DSA root certs, for nine cross-certs and 13 root certificate variants including four self-certs. ML-DSA root never signs a classical root by default. Cross-certs are path candidates, never trust anchors.

## Current evidence
V1 has no PKI. Exact graph is spec §§3.2/24.2 and source precedence.

## Acceptance/oracle
Enumerated manifest edge set equals the normative 9-edge table; every edge has correct subject SPKI, signer issuer/AKI, distinct serial/fingerprint, validity, signature algorithm and revocation owner. Verify with OpenSSL and an independent verifier for supported algorithms. Oracle is exact edge enumeration plus cryptographic verification.

## Negative tests
Forbidden ML-DSA-to-classical edge, wrong signer/AKI/SPKI, expired/substituted edge, duplicate serial, cross-cert accepted as trust anchor, or path that claims unsupported algorithm must fail.

## Rollback/safety
Revert/deactivate only synthetic graph version and retain evidence. Strict argument preflight before side effects; no production root signing or trust publication.

title: Enforce transaction-bound root signing authorization
stage: V2 synthetic policy tests; V3 authorized live signer
body:
## Outcome
Every root signature consumes transaction-bound `SigningAuthorization` bound to root key fingerprint/handle; subject public-key identity + signature algorithm; profile/purpose; exact validity; artifact-plan digest; authorized output/escrow destinations; expiry; transaction ID; single-use by default. Signer refuses mismatches and emits receipt naming the transaction. Inventory lookup, escrow read access or holding key bytes never mints authorization.

## Current evidence/status
V1 has no signer implementation; production signing is unauthorized. Implement synthetic policy tests in V2 only; live signer remains blocked pending explicit approval.

## Acceptance/oracle
A fake signer records invocation count and refuses before signature on any missing/mismatched grant; a matching synthetic authorization returns a transaction-bound receipt. Oracle: exact authorization-field comparison and zero signer calls/writes on denial.

## Negative tests
Ambient/default discovery, signer substitution, changed artifact digest, wrong purpose, altered validity, unauthorized destination, expired/replayed grant, escrow read treated as authority, key handle passed as ordinary secret ref, or grant rebound to another transaction all reject.

## Rollback/safety
No real signer or key bytes in V2. Production operation lifecycle is Blocked until approval/custody review. On failure preserve audit record and stop; never retry signature without idempotency proof. Operator scripts strictly validate argv before signer/store/network/file/lock side effects.

title: Generate Base and Internal Web A/B issuer keys and certificate graph
body:
## Outcome
Build Base and Internal Web synthetic issuer sets with independent A/B keys for each of the four algorithms. Apply the enumerated §24.2 direct signer matrix (13 certificates per purpose/partition, 26 per purpose, 52 total); reference expiry for both is `2032-07-07T12:00:00Z`. Ordinary profile expiry remains five calendar years. This issue owns CA graph integration under #9163; #9164 owns lifecycle and delivery workflows.

## Current evidence
No PKI in V1. Spec §24.2 is authoritative; the exact 32+20 prose split is reconciled separately in CERT-02 before implementation is considered complete.

## Acceptance/oracle
16 unique issuer keys; per purpose 8 keys and 26 certs; exact edge set; same-key cert variants retain SPKI/SKI but have distinct issuer/AKI/serial/signature/fingerprint; A/B have different SPKI/SKI; extension and validity profile verified independently. Oracle: signed graph manifest and independent verifier.

## Negative tests
No ML-DSA-root signature on classical issuer; no A/B or purpose key reuse; reject invalid pathLen, over-parent validity, duplicate issuer+serial, profile mismatch, unsupported OID and unauthorized root signer.

## Safety/rollback
Synthetic keys only. Roll back by deactivating only fixture generation and preserve serial/evidence; never touch production. Strict full argv validation before keygen/sign/network/write/lock. Root signing authorization is per operation.

title: Implement trust profiles and strict PQ-only path selection
body:
## Outcome
Generate roots-all, roots-classical and roots-pq bundles and deterministic candidate paths. Installable anchors are only selected self-signed roots; cross-certificates/intermediates stay untrusted. PQ-only requires ML-DSA root and ML-DSA signatures throughout; compatibility trust never claims PQ assurance.

## Current evidence
No Fleet trust feature exists in V1. Client algorithm support and trust stores are unverified per target/version.

## Acceptance/oracle
All-Ml-DSA synthetic path passes when verifier supports it; every classical leaf or any classical edge fails under PQ-only policy even if algorithm is supported. OpenSSL + independent Rust verifier results with pinned versions and actual chain bytes are the oracle; unsupported is not pass.

## Negative tests
Cross-cert as anchor, all-roots mislabeled PQ, classical fallback, unknown algorithm, invalid pathLen/AKI, unsupported signature and chain-order ambiguity reject.

## Rollback
Synthetic bundle/policy version can be deactivated; no auto-install. Trust installation is a separate privileged, approved operation. Strict arg parsing before installer/subprocess/privilege side effects.

title: Package public root artifacts and interoperable trust bundles
body:
## Outcome
Package public-only root bundles: manifest, PEM/DER, certs-only CMS when verified, trust subsets, cross-cert candidates, explicit chains, hashes and platform-specific install/verify/remove guidance. Do not duplicate leaf handoff format implementation; depend on #9164 CERT-12.

## Current evidence
V1 has no PKI artifact generation. Client installation capabilities vary; target/version claims must be evidenced.

## Acceptance/oracle
Public manifest/hash list matches exact bytes; PEM/DER consistency; CMS includes expected certs only; cross-certs are not trust anchors; OpenSSL and independent Rust validator agree on supported paths. Every guide is versioned or marked unverified.

## Negative tests
Reject private key in public archive, hash mismatch, wrong MIME/encoding, cross-cert in anchor bundle, unsupported client claimed supported, or SSH/X.509 confusion.

## Rollback/safety
Artifacts immutable by generation; rollback changes staged references, not bytes. No trust store changes or network publication. Strict argv validation before archive/filesystem/network action.

title: Build closed three-destination encrypted root escrow adapter
body:
## Outcome
Implement a dedicated closed `RootEscrowDestinations` type that allows exactly encrypted laptop storage, authorized BWS project, and authorized 1Password vault. It does not use the ordinary resolver, cache, prefetch, equality index, or generic replication policy. R2 remains research-only.

## Current evidence/status
The addendum requests these three destination classes but explicitly does not authorize production generation/export/write in this design run. Actual project/vault identity, permissions and recovery recipients are unverified. Remain Blocked pending explicit applicable approval.

## Acceptance/oracle
Synthetic encrypted fixture only until approved. Receipt for all three. Custody-complete only after all three are present and each independently restores with the other two unavailable; otherwise return incomplete. Verify recovered key fingerprint and a synthetic sign/verify; no plaintext in logs. Oracle: independent restore and exact fingerprint.

## Negative tests
Reject extra destination/provider, R2, plaintext archive, wrong project/vault, stale/corrupt archive, ordinary secret reference as root signer, incomplete receipts, ordinary cache/prefetch/equality index, permission denied, and recovery circularity.

## Rollback/safety
Production remains blocked. Stopping replication preserves every verified copy; never auto-delete. Strict full argv parse before vault/network/filesystem/lock operations. Authorization and repair are separate idempotent transactions; no assumption of portable CAS.

title: Specify independent root recovery and restoration rehearsal
stage: V3 synthetic restore; production approval gated
body:
## Outcome
Design and rehearse independent recovery of each root archive and full bundle. Recovery authority must be separate from the root key and each one provider/destination under test. Complete means all three approved destination copies restore independently with the other two unavailable.

## Current evidence/status
No production root archive or authorized recovery identities exist in this design task. Synthetic restoration only; live recovery remains Blocked until custody approval.

## Acceptance/oracle
Run separate synthetic cases for laptop loss, BWS unavailable, 1Password unavailable, archive corruption and recovery-recipient loss. Verify matching root SPKI/fingerprint, manifest integrity and test signing. Record exact dependencies and operator steps; oracle is recovery from each one remaining destination and independent credential without contacting the other two.

## Negative tests
Reject recovery relying on same provider being restored, recipient stored only inside its own encrypted archive, checksums without authenticated integrity, or incomplete three-copy status.

## Rollback
Destroy only synthetic fixtures after preserving nonsecret evidence. Never delete the last verified production copy; no production restore without explicit authorization and witness.

title: Design root lifecycle replacement and trust migration
body:
## Outcome
Specify root renew-vs-rotate-vs-replace, new-generation trust overlap, dependent issuer inventory, client migration, deprecation and archival recovery over the long root lifetime. Keep active signing authority distinct from escrow and design future offline/HSM/external-signer migration without claiming hardware exists.

## Current evidence
V1 has no PKI; hardware/offline signer is future design, not current capability. Existing cross-domain issue dependencies should be referenced, not duplicated.

## Acceptance/oracle
State model and synthetic migration rehearsal prove new key identity/generation on rotate/replace; renew revision may preserve key only by explicit policy; old root remains available until dependents and clients verified; all paths retain receipts/CRL/public artifacts.

## Negative tests
Reject silent key reuse, removal of trust before overlap, destruction of historical CRLs, unsupported recovery, and a design that assumes root public cert alone recovers private key.

## Rollback
Stop activation and return to prior trust package while valid; never reverse a signed event by deleting the root. Production ceremony separately approved.

title: Define production root ceremony and explicit approval gates
stage: V4 production ceremony only after owner authorization
body:
## Outcome
Produce a reviewed ceremony runbook/preflight for any eventual production root generation, signature, escrow, publication or trust action. It must bind transaction authorization to key fingerprint, subject SPKI/algorithm, purpose, exact validity, artifact-plan digest, authorized destinations, expiry, transaction ID and single-use default; enumerate exact three escrow destinations and independent restore checks.

## Current evidence/status
This design does not authorize production operations. Keep Blocked until the owner supplies explicit applicable approval, custody identities, reviewed rollback and independent witness.

## Acceptance/oracle
Synthetic dry-run emits exact artifacts/actions/approvals and proves no live side effect. Missing/expired/wrong-scope approval prevents signer invocation, store/network write, DNS or trust mutation. Preflight-to-apply evidence can demonstrate external edits are not overwritten under unguarded conflict-sensitive target; oracle is protected external value plus `needs_review`/conflict receipt.

## Negative tests
Ambient signer lookup, replayed grant, changed artifact digest, unauthorized destination, incomplete three-copy restore, broad `--yes`, unexplained unguarded write and partial mirror must stop.

## Rollback/safety
No live run under this issue unless separately authorized. Before signing, abort/no-op; after signing preserve key/certificate and evidence, halt publication and follow incident plan. Never claim key deletion reverses issuance. Strict complete argv parse before any side effect.

title: Define issuer and leaf typed profile/API contracts
source_ranges: spec §§3, 6, 24, 26; Appendix A PKI-009–018, PKI-027, PKI-052, PKI-057
body:
## Outcome
Design the PKI facade types for purpose, issuer set/key/cert identity, CSR/leaf request, signer authorization, receipt and injected clock/entropy/sink. This issue owns PKI-specific contracts only; shared CLI registry, secret identities and general provider framework remain in #9157/#9158.

## Current evidence
V1 has no Fleet `cert`/`pki` domain; this is a V1 design deliverable, not implementation. Interfaces in `pki-issuance.md` are proposals.

## Acceptance/oracle
Schema/type proposal has explicit error/state behavior, stable opaque IDs separate from paths, algorithm capability boundary and CLI-to-library parity. Golden normalization tests reject unknown purpose and ambiguous parent; JSON schema is validated. Oracle is deterministic type/schema fixtures.

## Negative tests
Reject name/path as object ID, silent default signer, unsupported algorithm, unregistered purpose, and inappropriate private data in public manifest.

## Rollback
Version the design/schema; do not migrate general Fleet credentials. Any operator utility uses strict whole-argv parsing before side effects.

title: Reconcile and freeze the 65-certificate signer graph
stage: V1 design decision; V2 immutable fixture
body:
## Outcome
Publish the complete explicit certificate edge manifest for 4 root keys/13 root certs and 16 issuer keys/52 issuer certs, 65 total before leaves. Resolve the assignment's `32 issuer cert variants + 20 direct intermediate cross certs` label against §24.2's exact matrix, which yields 13 per partition and 52 issuer cert entries. Do not silently drop eligible signer edges or mislabel counts.

## Current evidence
V1 has no PKI. The spec matrix is normative; the supplied task's 32+20 split is not uniquely derived by the table. `pki_graph.py` is a pure synthetic arithmetic oracle, not crypto evidence.

## Acceptance/oracle
Machine-readable row for every cert: subject opaque/key ID, signer root ID, algorithm, purpose/partition, cert role and eligibility. Assert 20 keys/65 certs, 4+9 root variants, 52 issuer variants, 13 per purpose/partition. Independent comparison to §§3.2/24.2 table.

## Negative tests
Reject missing/extra edge, duplicate identity, A/B alias, ML-DSA-root-to-classical, wrong 32+20 accounting, and any count-based test with no exact edge-set oracle.

## Rollback
Graph schema revisions are versioned; signed/published graph is never rewritten. Supersede with new graph version and preserve old evidence. Synthetic only; no signing or production changes.

title: Implement signer capability and explicit authorization contract
body:
## Outcome
Implement PKI signer adapter descriptor and transaction-bound authorization checks for synthetic signers. Root authorization binds key fingerprint/handle, subject SPKI ID + algorithm, profile/purpose, exact validity, artifact-plan digest, output/escrow destination set, expiry, transaction ID and single-use default.

## Current evidence
No V1 signer API. No production signer or authorization is available; interfaces are proposals.

## Acceptance/oracle
Exact TBS signing/verifying with synthetic adapter; receipt names authorization transaction. Fake signer invocation counter proves denied request is rejected before signing. Report each object type and scheme capability separately.

## Negative tests
Wrong key/signer, algorithm, subject, purpose, validity, digest, destination, expired/replayed transaction, escrow read access as authority, handle as ordinary secret ref, and fallback signer must reject.

## Rollback
Synthetic adapter feature can be disabled; preserve receipts. Production signer integration requires separate approved issue and custody gate; no keys in ordinary cache/prefetch/benchmark/equality index.

title: Build strict CSR parser and proof-of-possession validator
source_ranges: spec §§10, 24; Appendix A PKI-014, PKI-026, PKI-045; RFC 2986
body:
## Outcome
Add bounded PKCS#10 DER/PEM CSR inspection and PoP verification. CSR subject, SPKI, SAN and extension requests are untrusted proposals; issuer policy creates final extensions. This is PKI parser work only, not general artifact import.

## Current evidence
No Fleet PKI in V1; RFC 2986 defines CSR shape and PoP, not CA issuance policy.

## Acceptance/oracle
Known-good synthetic CSR accepted; parsed SPKI matches eventual cert; OpenSSL independently inspects/validates fixture. Parse bounds and typed errors; no signer invocation during invalid preflight.

## Negative tests
Malformed/oversized DER, invalid PoP, unknown critical extension/OID, duplicate extension, unsupported parameters, path traversal filename, requested SAN outside policy and SPKI mismatch reject before signer.

## Rollback
No raw CSR persistence by default; remove only operation-owned test file. Strict CLI arguments before file/network/signer side effects.

title: Define purpose profiles, extension policy, and SAN/wildcard validator
body:
## Outcome
Implement Base/InternalWeb typed profiles, certificate KU/EKU/pathLen/name constraints, SAN normalization, and wildcard validation. Web apex+wildcard shorthand yields four exact names for the two reference domains. Public trust is not implied by public DNS.

## Current evidence
No V1 PKI. RFC 9525 requires full leftmost wildcard semantics; client enforcement of name constraints varies and must be tested.

## Acceptance/oracle
Canonical SAN list/property tests, pinned public-suffix test data, independent hostname verifier; Web uses serverAuth and SAN; no CN fallback. Oracle: expected normalized identities and target verifier result.

## Negative tests
Reject multi-label/multiple wildcard, embedded `*`, wildcard IP/URI/email, public suffix, malformed IDNA, constrained-out SAN, CN-only hostname, excessive KU/EKU and algorithm-incompatible usage.

## Rollback
Profiles are immutable/versioned; correct via new version. Synthetic only. Strict argument validation before signer or output side effects.

title: Implement issuer-set synthetic builder and graph verification
body:
## Outcome
Generate synthetic Base and InternalWeb issuer A/B keys and their frozen certificate graph; produce manifest and deterministic artifacts. #9163 owns root inventory/custody; this issue owns the issuer builder.

## Current evidence
No Fleet PKI in V1. Graph and exact 32+20 reconciliation must close in CERT-02 before the fixture is accepted.

## Acceptance/oracle
16 unique issuer keys; 52 cert variants under approved graph; expiry both sets `2032-07-07T12:00:00Z`; correct CA extensions, subject, SKI/AKI, serial ledger, signer authorization and signatures independently validated.

## Negative tests
Forbidden ML-DSA-root/classical issuer, duplicate A/B or purpose key, validity beyond root, wrong key usage/pathLen, profile drift, duplicate serial, missing CRL prerequisite, signer authorization mismatch.

## Rollback
Synthetic operation-owned fixtures only; retain serial gaps and failure receipt. No production signer/store/publication. Strict complete argv parse before keygen/sign/write/lock/network.

title: Implement leaf issuance API/CLI and fast in-memory mode
body:
## Outcome
Issue synthetic Base test leaf and InternalWeb leaf through the same typed library and Fleet CLI contract. Fast mode returns in-memory artifacts without documentation or network work. Multiple selected algorithms produce separate keys/certs, never one multialgorithm cert.

## Current evidence
No V1 Fleet PKI. CLI names/examples in source are proposed, not executable commands.

## Acceptance/oracle
Base 1y test identity and Web SAN leaf; exact SPKI and chain; validity bounded by parent; API/CLI output oracle agrees. Private key remains in test handle by default. Verify with OpenSSL plus independent Rust verifier where supported.

## Negative tests
Web no SAN, CSR unauthorized SAN, invalid wildcard, expired parent, leaf expiry beyond issuer, unavailable algorithm, key/signature mismatch, private key in public-only output, and PQ policy fallback reject.

## Rollback
Stage only synthetic artifacts; retain previous fixture until new is verified. Strict whole-argv parse before signer/output/network/lock side effects.

title: Add renew/rotate/replace state and safe resume
stage: V2 synthetic lifecycle, V3 guarded activation
body:
## Outcome
Implement distinct cert renew/reissue, key rotate, and orchestrated replace states with resumable receipts. Renew preserves key only under explicit policy and increments cert revision/serial; rotate creates independent key and generation.

## Current evidence
No V1 implementation. Spec §5.2 distinguishes lifecycle terms and requires trust overlap.

## Acceptance/oracle
Synthetic state-model tests prove identity/revision transitions, idempotent resume, no double signing, and new generation trust plan; exact manifest IDs are oracle. Inject interruption at every stage.

## Negative tests
Reject silent key reuse on rotate, claim of rotation without new SPKI, expiry beyond parent, retry with changed request hash, removal of old trust before verified overlap.

## Rollback
Before activation cancel; after signing preserve artifacts/serial evidence; after publication do not delete immutable objects; use explicit alias/trust overlap recovery. No production operation without approval.

title: Build CRL state, signing, and lifecycle ledger
body:
## Outcome
Implement synthetic per-signing-CA revocation ledger and signed CRL build/verify. Root CRLs cover issuer and root-cross certs signed by that root; issuer CRLs cover leaves. Create a real signed empty CRL before any CDP-bearing cert becomes publishable.

## Current evidence
No live CRLs or endpoint. Spec §§4.3/24.7 require correct signer-specific status and initial CRL. OCSP is separately deferred.

## Acceptance/oracle
Monotonic issuer-specific CRL number, signed thisUpdate/nextUpdate, correct issuer/AKI, only authorized serial membership; OpenSSL and independent verifier validate signature, and publication manifest hashes exact bytes.

## Negative tests
Wrong signer/CRL owner, stale CRL, duplicate serial/CRL number, missing empty CRL, unauthorized revoke, phantom `good`, root cross-cert on subject rather than signer CRL.

## Rollback
Revocation is append-only; correct with next CRL, never remove historical CRL/entry as rollback. Production revoke/sign/publish remains approval-gated; strict argv before signer/network/write/lock.

title: Construct AIA/CDP and immutable publication plans
body:
## Outcome
Build URI and artifact publication plans with immutable object paths, exact relative source, destination, content type, hash, visibility, cache policy and mirror state. Leaf AIA names issuer candidates; CDP names actual signer's CRL; cross-signed CA AIA/CDP point to signing root artifacts.

## Current evidence
`pki.developing.today` is illustrative, not verified deployed. AIA retrieval is opportunistic. No network publication is authorized.

## Acceptance/oracle
Local HTTP fixtures return exact bytes/MIME/hashes for DER, CRL, CMS; CRL exists before `publishable`; mirror hashes equal where configured; URI parser extensions match manifest issuer IDs. Oracle is fetched bytes+cryptographic checks.

## Negative tests
Bare directory URI, mutable old path, wrong issuer, missing CRL, false OCSP URI, bad MIME, HTTPS bootstrap redirect, auth barrier, wrong mirror bytes and path traversal reject.

## Rollback
Staged local artifacts only; production paths immutable. Failure retains partial receipt for safe resume; no DNS change. Strict argument validation before any network/file/lock action.

title: Add atomic staged publication and guarded alias updates
stage: V2 local/mock publisher; V3 separately approved deploy
body:
## Outcome
Implement publication state/receipts for immutable object creation and controlled aliases. For every adapter+operation declare guard level `atomic-precondition | serialized-by-contract | unguarded`. Until primary docs plus isolated test prove otherwise BWS/op/bw are unguarded. Conflict-sensitive writes require first or second guard; Fleet lease/readback is not serialization. Unguarded target stops `needs_review` unless separately approved named weaker policy records lost-update window in plan and receipt. Additive immutable creates/history are not gated.

## Acceptance/oracle
Fault-injection test preflight → external edit → apply: external value remains recoverable and operation reports conflict. Local publisher tests partial upload, hash/MIME mismatch, alias race and retry. Only use CAS where provider/version documents and proves it. Oracle: preserved competing value plus conflict receipt, not lock/readback.

## Negative tests
Reject assumed CAS, Fleet lease represented as serialization, silent overwrite, lost-update policy without named approval/window, overwrite at immutable path, and retry without idempotency key.

## Rollback/safety
No production publish in V2. Published objects are immutable; rollback uses guard-appropriate alias recovery and reports cache residuals. Strict argv parse before network/write/lock/deploy.

title: Implement certificates-only CMS and delivery kit formats
body:
## Outcome
Produce PEM/DER, certs-only CMS/P7C and precomposed chain artifacts for minimal/public-only/handoff kits. Private formats require a separately authorized encrypted destination; SSH/PGP/JWT stay native and separate.

## Current evidence
No Fleet kit implementation in V1. RFC 5652 defines CMS structure; Rust crate docs do not alone prove full workflow.

## Acceptance/oracle
CMS parser verifies degenerate SignedData/no signers and expected certificate fingerprints; DER/PEM roundtrip exact certs; chain order and MIME match manifest. Independent parser/verifier tests and corpus are oracle.

## Negative tests
Reject signed CMS mistaken as certs-only, unexpected cert/private key, wrong MIME, chain rooted in untrusted cross-cert as anchor, unsupported format/algorithm, `.crt` extension assumed to mean DER, SSH certificate represented as X.509.

## Rollback
Artifacts are versioned and immutable; revert kit pointer, never overwrite. No private export or production distribution; strict args before archive/file operations.

title: Implement trust-profile export, install plan, and test matrix
stage: V2 synthetic export/test; V3 install approval
body:
## Outcome
Export roots-all/classical/PQ bundles and explicit install plans by OS/client. Cross-certs and intermediates are untrusted path candidates. This owns #9164 trust handoff; root graph belongs to #9163.

## Current evidence
V1 has no trust installer. Client and algorithm support unverified; docs must name versions and mark unsupported accurately.

## Acceptance/oracle
Independent OpenSSL and Rust path verification with explicit chains; PQ-only accepts all-ML-DSA path and rejects any classical leaf/signature; all-roots never labeled PQ. Install plan is non-mutating; where testable target client confirms fingerprints.

## Negative tests
Cross-cert imported as anchor, unsupported client success claim, automatic global trust modification, malformed chain, classical fallback in PQ profile, and SSH/X.509 conflation.

## Rollback
Export-only is safe. Install is separate privileged approved action with exact fingerprint and scope; removal plan touches only installed fingerprints and maintains overlap.

title: Keep OCSP explicitly unsupported unless responder is complete
source_ranges: spec §§4.3, 24.7, 33.2, 48.2 V3-S22; Appendix A PKI-033, PKI2-022; RFC 6960; note.md unsupported class
stage: V1 design decision; V2 negative capability test
body:
## Outcome
Keep OCSP URI absent and capability explicitly unsupported unless a real responder has issuer routing, status DB, authorization, key custody, freshness, rate limits, request validation, audit and independent tests for each issuer/algorithm. OpenBao ML-DSA limitation remains unsupported, not an alternate success path.

## Current evidence
No OCSP endpoint exists in V1. RFC 6960 `good` does not prove issuance. Research note records crate ASN.1 support as distinct from operational responder support.

## Acceptance/oracle
Capability output says unsupported; no OCSP AIA extension when service is absent. Fake query for unknown issuer/algorithm never returns synthetic `good`; implement RFC state distinctions and tests only if future responder separately approved.

## Negative tests
Phantom URL, `good` from absence in stale CRL, responder key unauthorized, issuer routing confusion, unsupported ML-DSA response, wrong freshness and no status DB all fail closed.

## Rollback
Keep feature disabled; removing unused capability has no production effect. Any future responder is a new reviewed issue, never part of this ticket's scope.

title: Generate DNS and publication runbooks without applying them
body:
## Outcome
Generate validated BIND zone fragment plus provider-neutral DNS/publication change manifest and PUBLISH/README instructions with relative source paths, exact target URLs, MIME, hashes, cache/revocation notes, validation and rollback. Generation never applies DNS.

## Current evidence
No domain record or PKI distribution host verified; `pki.*` names are proposed placeholders. CAA authorizes public CA issuance, not private CA. CT is generally public WebPKI; private CA has its own ledger.

## Acceptance/oracle
Zone parser and schema validate; every plan path maps to a generated artifact; unresolved placeholders cannot execute. Docs distinguish ACME/DCV/CAA/CT and private trust. Oracle is parser + file/URL/hash consistency.

## Negative tests
Invalid zone syntax, placeholder treated as live, fabricated DNS diff, private CA described as browser-public, CAA treated as private CA authorization, and DNS mutation in generation tests reject.

## Rollback
Docs/plan files are versioned; no DNS operation exists. Strict args before file/network actions.

title: Add issuance state, journaling, and failure recovery
body:
## Outcome
Implement append-only issuance operation states, request hashes, actor/approval, signer receipt, artifact hash, idempotency and resumable batch state. Own PKI lifecycle receipts, not the general Fleet journal/outbox.

## Current evidence
V1 PKI absent. Architecture ADR-S02 says hosted adapters may lack CAS; Fleet leases/readback are not serialization. Declare per-adapter/per-operation guard level. BWS/op/bw are unguarded until primary evidence + isolated test prove otherwise.

## Acceptance/oracle
Inject failure before signer, after signer, CRL build, staging, upload, alias, and activation. On conflict-sensitive unguarded write, plan stops `needs_review` unless named approved weaker policy states lost-update window in plan+receipt. Oracle preflight → external edit → apply: external value recoverable and conflict reported.

## Negative tests
No serial reuse, duplicate signature, false active status, blind retry after uncertain timeout, lease called serialization, or overwrite after concurrent edit. Additive immutable creates/history remain allowed.

## Rollback
Preserve signed/published evidence, resume by exact request hash/receipt, never delete immutable artifacts; strict whole argv before all side effects.

title: Prove backend compatibility and independent validation per artifact
source_ranges: spec §§9, 11.2, 35, 48; Appendix A PKI-061–064, PKI-070, PKI-074; research/pki-standards.md
body:
## Outcome
Maintain version-pinned capability evidence for rcgen, x509-cert/RustCrypto, OpenSSL and independent path verifiers by algorithm and object type: cert, CSR, CRL, CMS, external signer. Recheck before dependency adoption.

## Current evidence
`research/pki-standards.md` has retrieved RFC and docs.rs capability boundaries; it is not proof that any crate supports the complete Fleet graph or is integrated.

## Acceptance/oracle
Per-operation table cites primary docs/source, versions, enabled features/platform, executable safe fixture and independent verifier output. Unsupported capability clearly marked unsupported. Oracle is executable output plus independently validated signature/profile.

## Negative tests
Do not infer signing from ASN.1 parser; path validation from DER parsing; HSM support from trait shape; ML-DSA from Dilithium; or complete issuance from library name. Reject silent substitution.

## Rollback
No prod dependencies or key operations. Version bump invalidates evidence and reruns corpus; remove optional adapter feature while preserving interface.

title: Stage guarded production issuance and publication approvals
body:
## Outcome
Design approval policy for scoped issuance, publication and trust operations. Bind every root signature to transaction `SigningAuthorization`; restrict root escrow to closed three-destination policy. Model adapter-operation guard level and halt conflict-sensitive unguarded apply unless separately approved named weaker policy carries lost-update window in plan+receipt.

## Current evidence/status
No live root signer, vault permission, DNS target or trust install is authorized. This issue remains Blocked. Synthetic dry-run may validate policy but cannot self-authorize production.

## Acceptance/oracle
Preflight displays exact objects, signer, authorization, destinations and effects. Missing/expired/wrong-scope approval produces zero signer/provider/network calls. Conflict injection preserves external edit and reports conflict. Publication only starts after independent verify and CRL readiness.

## Negative tests
Ambient signing, replayed authorization, unknown escrow destination, incomplete restore, unguarded overwrite, `--force` bypass, stale/missing CRL, and auto trust/DNS mutation all block.

## Rollback
Before signing no-op; after signature preserve artifacts/audit, do not claim reversal; post-publication immutable objects remain and alias rollback is guard-capability dependent. Never operate without separately documented owner authorization.

title: Prepare offline and hardware signer migration rehearsal
source_ranges: spec §§24.3, 33.3, 40, 48; addendum §5; Appendix A PKI-044, PKI-071, PKI-074
body:
## Outcome
Research and rehearse an adapter migration from temporary approved custody to offline/HSM/PKCS#11/KMS/external signer, preserving explicit transaction-bound authorization, historic roots, recovery and trust overlap. No hardware capability is claimed now.

## Current evidence
V1 has no Fleet PKI or verified HSM. Addendum asks for future offline/hardware path; architecture review ADR-S05 requires independent restoration.

## Acceptance/oracle
Synthetic migration verifies public key identity/fingerprint, exact TBS signature and receipt across adapter change; outage/restore, new/old trust overlap and independent archive recovery rehearsed. Source-backed capability matrix distinguishes hardware-tested from API-theoretical support.

## Negative tests
Reject implicit signer fallback, key export without approval, root handle used as ordinary secret, unsupported attestation claim, changed subject key, removal of old root before dependent-client proof.

## Rollback
Return only to a still-authorized prior signer and preserve trust overlap; no production migration without separate approval. Research is nonblocking for V2 synthetic graph.
